From Puckline Press

Puckline Press article

Frozen Frenzy, explained: the night all 32 NHL teams play

Tuesday's 16-game Frozen Frenzy was the fourth in a row. Here's what the event is, where it came from, how rare it is, and how last night went.

By Puckline Prince · Oct 14, 2026 · Article page

Read the article

Every NHL team played on Tuesday night. That's the Frozen Frenzy: one evening, 16 games, all 32 clubs, and a new puck drop almost every 15 minutes from 6 p.m. Eastern until the last game started at 11. ESPN says this was the fourth year in a row it has put the event on.

The Frozen Frenzy is a scheduling showcase built with ESPN. The league gives the night a full slate, then spreads the start times out so the games overlap as little as possible. ESPN carries a tripleheader on its main channel (6 p.m., 8:30 p.m. and 11 p.m. Eastern), and the other 13 games stream on its services.

The centrepiece is a whip-around studio show that jumps from rink to rink for goals, big hits and late finishes, the hockey version of the NFL's RedZone. In the first edition, John Buccigross and Kevin Weekes hosted it, and the show ran about six and a half hours across ESPN+ and ESPN2.

This year's tripleheader was Devils at Red Wings at 6, Avalanche at Stars at 8:30 and Bruins at Sharks at 11. The other games started every 15 minutes from 6:15 to 9 p.m., then at 9:45 (Flames at Ducks) and 10:30 (Oilers at Kings), so all 16 games had their own start time.

A night with all 32 teams in action is newer than you might think. The first 16-game day in NHL history was Saturday, April 8, 2023, the last Saturday of the 2022-23 regular season. That day started at 12:30 p.m. Eastern and was not branded as anything.

The first Frozen Frenzy came six months later, on Tuesday, Oct. 24, 2023. NHL.com called it the second 16-game day in league history. ESPN's tripleheader that night was Maple Leafs at Capitals, Bruins at Blackhawks (Connor Bedard's rookie season) and Flyers at the Golden Knights, the defending Stanley Cup champions.

Since then it has become a fixture of October:

  • Oct. 24, 2023: the first Frozen Frenzy
  • Oct. 22, 2024: opened with Capitals at Flyers, closed with Kings at Golden Knights
  • Oct. 28, 2025: opened with Penguins at Flyers, closed with Kings at Sharks
  • Oct. 13, 2026: opened with Devils at Red Wings, closed with Bruins at Sharks

All four have been on a Tuesday.

Nights like this are rare. Before the 2024 edition, NHL.com counted only three earlier days with all 32 teams playing: April 8, 2023, the first Frozen Frenzy, and Jan. 13, 2024. It also said the 2024 Frenzy would be the only day that season with every team in action.

So the Frenzy is the one guaranteed 16-game night on the calendar, and in some seasons it has been the only one.

The 2026 edition delivered 112 goals in 16 games, an average of seven a game. Road teams won nine of the 16. Three games went past regulation: the Devils won in overtime in Detroit, 5-4, and the Canadiens (over Buffalo, 4-3) and Kraken (in Philadelphia, 3-2) both won in shootouts.

All the final scores:

  • Devils 5, Red Wings 4 (OT)
  • Panthers 7, Blue Jackets 3
  • Canadiens 4, Sabres 3 (SO)
  • Hurricanes 4, Capitals 2
  • Kraken 3, Flyers 2 (SO)
  • Rangers 4, Lightning 1
  • Blues 7, Senators 2
  • Islanders 3, Canucks 2
  • Blackhawks 5, Penguins 3
  • Jets 5, Wild 2
  • Avalanche 3, Stars 2
  • Golden Knights 5, Predators 2
  • Mammoth 5, Maple Leafs 4
  • Flames 4, Ducks 2
  • Oilers 4, Kings 1
  • Bruins 6, Sharks 3

The most lopsided results were Florida's 7-3 win in Columbus and St. Louis's 7-2 win in Ottawa. In the 8:30 headliner, Colorado beat Dallas 3-2 in regulation, and Boston closed the night with six goals in San Jose.

Full recaps of every game are on the Last night page.

Tuesday, October 20

Game recap

ANA2NYR5Final: ANA 2, NYR 5

The Rangers keep treating Madison Square Garden like a members-only club, and Anaheim wasn't on the list: 5-2, and New York is 6-0 at home. Sean Durzi scored 78 seconds in, J.T. Miller added a power-play goal, Gabe Perreault made it 3-0, and Oliver Bjorkstrand scored twice in barely 12 minutes of ice time, the kind of efficiency Rangers fans usually only see at the ticket office. Alexis Lafrenière set up two, and Dylan Garand stopped 29 of 31 to keep the Shesterkin-less crease humming. Ville Husso made 25 saves on 30. The Ducks finally scored at 18:51 of the third, then again at 19:27 through A.J. Greer, two goals that changed nothing but the box score. That's three straight losses for Anaheim, a team that flew across the country to watch a show and forgot it was supposed to be in it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL2PHI3Final: COL 2, PHI 3

Philadelphia scores 1.40 goals a game, so naturally it hung three on one of the highest-scoring teams in the league. Flyers 3, Avalanche 2, and that's two wins in three nights for a team that couldn't buy one for two weeks. Matvei Michkov scored twice, the first on the power play, and Trevor Zegras set up all three Flyers goals, including Noel Acciari's first of the season early in the third. Joseph Woll stopped 24 of 26, which is all Colorado managed to throw at him, and Nathan MacKinnon went 24 minutes without a point. Martin Necas and T.J. Hughes scored for the Avs, Hughes with five minutes left, but Mackenzie Blackwood (21 saves on 24) got no more help. A Philly lineup missing Tippett, Konecny and York did this. Colorado now flies to New Jersey to play again tonight, which is still a better trip than the one its offense just took.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS1TOR3Final: SJS 1, TOR 3

The Maple Leafs finally stopped the bleeding, and it took a teenager to do it. Toronto beat San Jose 3-1 to end a three-game skid. Mason Marchment put the Sharks up in the first, Auston Matthews tied it on the power play with 12 seconds left in the second, and Gavin McKenna scored the winner on another power play early in the third, his third of the year. Nick Paul hit the empty net with 40 seconds left. Matthews finished with a goal and two assists, William Nylander shook off an illness to set up the winner, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 30 of 31. Yaroslav Askarov was excellent in a losing cause, 29 saves on 31, and Macklin Celebrini put five shots on goal for nothing. The Sharks are 4-4-1 and still haven't won a game in regulation: nine games in, and they're still waiting for a win that doesn't need extra time or a skills competition.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT4UTA5Final: PIT 4, UTA 5

Erik Karlsson finally scored a goal, and Pittsburgh still found a way to lose. His power-play goal 71 seconds in was his first of the season, and the Penguins promptly gave up five of the next six as Utah won 5-4. Clayton Keller, Kevin Stenlund, Nate Schmidt, Kailer Yamamoto and Nick Schmaltz scored for Utah, Schmaltz on the power play early in the third for a 5-2 lead. Then the Penguins remembered they had shooters: Egor Chinakhov and Declan Carlile made it 5-4 with five minutes left, and that was it. Utah outshot Pittsburgh 29-19, so Sebastian Cossa only had to stop 15 of 19, while Arturs Silovs made 24 saves on 29. Bryan Rust had two assists before leaving with a lower-body injury. That's four straight losses and a 3-6-1 record for a team built to squeeze one more run out of Sid and Geno, and so far the only thing it's squeezing is the panic button.

Monday, October 19

Game recap

CBJ1MIN2Final: CBJ 1, MIN 2

Columbus came to St. Paul, put 14 shots on goal in 60 minutes and somehow left with a 2-1 loss instead of a shutout, which tells you everything about Cam Talbot. Talbot stopped 32 of 34 and kept a lopsided night close. Danila Yurov opened it with 1:48 left in the first, Adam Fantilli answered a minute later with Talbot pulled for an extra attacker, and then Kirill Kaprizov did the Kaprizov thing on the power play 3:06 into the second: his 10th of the season, most in the league. After that, nobody scored for 37 minutes and Jesper Wallstedt got through his 13 saves without breaking a sweat. Minnesota is 6-2-1, in first place in the Central, and doing it without Brock Faber, Jared Spurgeon or either Foligno in the lineup. Columbus is 3-4-0 and averaged a shot every four minutes and change. You can't score on chances you don't take, and the Blue Jackets aren't taking any.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR2CGY3Final: CAR 2, CGY 3

Carolina rolled into Calgary on a seven-game win streak and ran into a team that had won once all season. The Flames won 3-2, only their second win of the season. Jesperi Kotkaniemi opened the scoring in the second, Matvei Gridin tied it with his first of the season, and Morgan Frost put Calgary ahead on the power play with 21 seconds left in the period. Jalen Chatfield tied it again with four seconds left, because the second period apparently had a closing-time rush. Then Yegor Sharangovich won it at 15:32 of the third, with Frost picking up his second point. Devin Cooley made 34 saves on 36 shots, Brandon Bussi 31 on 34, and Nicolas Deslauriers, a late call into the lineup, set up the first goal. Carolina is still 7-2-1 and first in the Metro. Calgary is 2-6-0, and one win over a good team doesn't make a rebuild, it just makes Monday less painful.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, October 18

Game recap

NJD2WSH4Final: NJD 2, WSH 4

New Jersey led for about six minutes, which is about as long as anything good lasts in Jersey traffic. Arseny Gritsyuk opened the scoring in the first, Ryan Leonard tied it on the power play (Logan Thompson picked up an assist, because why not), and then Washington scored three times in the first 11:14 of the second: Ilya Protas off an Alex Ovechkin feed, Dylan Strome, and Boone Jenner. Vincent Desharnais, not a name that usually shows up in a box score, had two assists. Thompson stopped 29 of 31; Jake Allen saw 25 shots and let in four. Timo Meier finally got his first of the season on a power play with 19 seconds left, the hockey version of finding a twenty in the couch after the rent bounced. The Devils are 4-4-0, and Jack Hughes' night was four shots, no points and 38% on draws. Somebody check whether the Devils' top line made the flight.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR3WPG2Final: CAR 3, WPG 2

Nothing hurts quite like a former Jet beating you on your own power play. Winnipeg led twice in the second, on a Mark Scheifele solo goal and Alex Iafallo off an Adam Lowry feed, and Carolina answered both: Mark Jankowski on the power play (his sixth already, so somebody alert the scouts) and Jesperi Kotkaniemi with his first of the season. Then, 6:43 into the third, Nikolaj Ehlers buried the power-play winner, set up by Shayne Gostisbehere, who had two assists. Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 21 saves on 23 shots. Clay Stevenson was the busy one in the other crease, 34 saves on 37, which is what happens when your Vezina goalie is still holding out. Carolina is 7-1-1 and has won seven straight. Winnipeg is 4-2-2, and every night Hellebuyck stays away the Jets' goalie budget looks a little more like a coupon book.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2TBL4Final: VAN 2, TBL 4

Vancouver led 2-0 in Tampa, which is a sentence that should come with a warning label. Linus Karlsson scored in the first and Elias Pettersson added one on the power play early in the second, and then Nikita Kucherov decided he'd seen enough. He scored on the power play two minutes later and again at 11:23 to tie it, moving into a tie with Marian Hossa for 65th on the NHL's career points list. Jake Guentzel put Tampa Bay ahead 2:04 into the third and Pontus Holmberg added insurance on his own. Dennis Hildeby got the win with 12 saves on 14 shots, a light shift by any standard. Kevin Lankinen made 31 saves and still lost. The Lightning are 6-2-0. The Canucks are 2-7-1, and a 2-0 lead in their hands is less a cushion than a countdown.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA3FLA8Final: SEA 3, FLA 8

Two hat tricks in one night, and Seattle paid for every hat. Carter Verhaeghe scored three times in a span of 8:06 across the first and second periods, and Sam Bennett bookended the night with three of his own, in only 12:25 of ice time. Matthew Tkachuk had three assists, brother Brady had two, and Niko Mikkola and Sam Reinhart chipped in a goal and an assist each, because by the second period everyone in red was getting a turn. Florida scored twice on the power play and outshot Seattle 37-23. Joey Daccord faced all 37 and stopped 29; Jacob Markstrom made 20 saves. Shane Wright, Frederick Gaudreau and Ryker Evans scored for the Kraken, and rookie Berkly Catton had two assists. Florida is 5-2-2. Seattle is 5-3-1 and leaves South Florida with the kind of souvenir nobody wants: eight goals against and a pile of hats.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI4TOR1Final: NYI 4, TOR 1

Ilya Sorokin walked into Scotiabank Arena and turned it into a library. He stopped 28 of 29 shots, the only one that got by him a Colton Sissons goal early in the third that briefly made it 2-1. Anthony Duclair opened the scoring in the first, Bo Horvat made it 2-0 late in the second, and Simon Holmstrom scored twice in the third, the second into an empty net. Horvat had a goal and an assist and played 24:21, and Matthew Schaefer picked up another helper. Sergei Bobrovsky allowed three goals on 19 shots. Auston Matthews' six-game point streak is over, and so, apparently, is Toronto's interest in winning: the Leafs have lost five of their last six and sit at 3-4-2. The Islanders are 4-3-1. In Toronto, the October panic is right on schedule, which is more than the offense can say.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3MTL4OTFinal: BUF 3, MTL 4 OT

Buffalo keeps coming to Montreal to donate points past regulation. Josh Norris put the Sabres up in the first, then Zachary Bolduc (power play), Cole Caufield and Alexandre Texier, with his first of the season, made it 3-1 Montreal. Jack Quinn scored shorthanded and Tage Thompson tied it midway through the third, which for one shining moment looked like character. Then Caufield needed 54 seconds of overtime to score his second of the night and the 14th overtime winner of his career. Alexandre Carrier and Juraj Slafkovsky had two assists each, Jacob Fowler made 23 saves, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 30. Oliver Kapanen and David Reinbacher made their season debuts for the Canadiens. Montreal is 4-3-1. Buffalo is 4-3-2, has now lost to the Habs in a shootout and in overtime this season, and is getting really good at almost.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS3DET4SOFinal: SJS 3, DET 4 SO

San Jose has found a brand-new way to lose, and it's the same way as last game. The Sharks led 3-1 in the third on goals from Dmitry Orlov (power play), Macklin Celebrini and Ivar Stenberg (power play), with Celebrini piling up three points, his 23rd three-point game, the eighth player in NHL history with that many before turning 21. Emmitt Finnie got one back, and then Alex DeBrincat tied it 6-on-5 with 1:33 left: the second straight game the Sharks gave up a tying goal with the other goalie on the bench. Lucas Raymond scored the only goal of the shootout. John Gibson made 31 saves, Alex Nedeljkovic 24, and Keegan Kolesar and Barclay Goodrow fought in the first. Detroit is 3-3-2. The Sharks are 4-3-1, and their late-game defense is less a shell than a welcome mat.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT1PHI3Final: OTT 1, PHI 3

Somebody tell Broad Street to stop holding its breath: the Flyers have won a hockey game. Ten games in, Philadelphia got its first win of the season, and the kids did it. Drake Batherson gave Ottawa a 1-0 lead early in the second, then rookie Porter Martone tied it off a Matvei Michkov feed, and Michkov returned the favour on the power play late in the period, each finishing with a goal and an assist. Trevor Zegras iced it into an empty net with 14 seconds left. Dan Vladar stopped 25 of 26, and Linus Ullmark made 25 saves on 27 in the loss. Ottawa lost Thomas Chabot to an upper-body injury after the second period. The Flyers are 1-6-3 and the parade route is being drawn up as we speak. The Senators are 6-3-0 and just lost to the only team that hadn't beaten anybody.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR0CBJ1OTFinal: NYR 0, CBJ 1 OT

Sixty minutes, zero goals, and somehow the most exciting thing in Columbus was the goaltending. Jet Greaves stopped all 29 Rangers shots for the shutout, and Dylan Garand matched him save for save until overtime, finishing with 28 on 29. Then, 3:26 into the extra frame, Kent Johnson finished it off a Zach Werenski and Charlie Coyle setup for his fourth goal of the season, and the Blue Jackets got two points out of a game that had all the scoring of a Tuesday afternoon board meeting. Columbus is 3-3-0 and gets right back at it in Minnesota tonight. The Rangers are 6-3-1, and 29 shots without a goal is the kind of night that makes a Broadway crowd start booing the Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL4CHI0Final: DAL 4, CHI 0

Jake Oettinger has now posted three shutouts before Halloween, and Chicago was happy to help. He stopped all 19 shots, which works out to roughly one every three minutes, a pace that let him plan his week between saves. Jason Robertson opened the scoring on a power play in the second, off a Mikko Rantanen feed, and added an assist. Arttu Hyry scored twice, once in the second and again 1:27 into the third, in only 12 minutes of ice time, and Roope Hintz finished it off. Spencer Knight made 28 saves on 32 and deserved a better team in front of him. Kevin Korchinski watched from the press box again. Dallas is 4-3-1. The Blackhawks are 3-6-0, and Chicago keeps buying the rebuild while the house keeps winning.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL2NSH5Final: STL 2, NSH 5

Nashville finally remembered it has a couple of very expensive forwards. Philip Broberg gave St. Louis a 1-0 lead early, Jonathan Marchessault tied it with an extra attacker on, and Filip Forsberg scored his first of the season off a Steven Stamkos feed. Adam Edstrom scored shorthanded in the second, Jimmy Snuggerud answered on the power play 31 seconds later, and then Ryan O'Reilly and Jack Drury pulled away in the third. Stamkos, Roman Josi and Adam Wilsby had two assists apiece, and Forsberg had a goal and an assist. Juuse Saros made 24 saves on 26. Jordan Binnington allowed five on 24 and played like a man counting down to the bus. Nashville is 3-2-3. The Blues are 3-4-1, and their defense spent the night giving Music City the kind of encore nobody paid for.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS4LAK1Final: BOS 4, LAK 1

The Kings scored 31 seconds in, and for the next 22 minutes, Los Angeles believed. Alex Laferriere finished off an Adrian Kempe and Brandt Clarke play, and then Boston did what Boston has been doing all week. David Pastrnak tied it on his own early in the second, Marat Khusnutdinov broke the tie with 6:24 left in the third, and Elias Lindholm and JJ Peterka put two into the empty net. Pastrnak and Khusnutdinov had a goal and an assist each, and Jeremy Swayman stopped 25 of 26. Anton Forsberg made 24 saves on 26. Mark Kastelic and Samuel Helenius fought late in the first. Boston is 7-2-0 with five straight wins and a sweep of the California trip. The Kings are 0-4-2, six games without a win, and the only thing Hollywood has scripted worse this fall is a sequel nobody asked for.

Game recap

EDM6UTA2Final: EDM 6, UTA 2

Connor McDavid scored 40 seconds in and then spent the rest of the night making Utah's defense look like it was skating in sand. He finished with two goals and three assists, stretching his season-opening point streak to eight games and his league-leading total to 23 points; his assists tie Wayne Gretzky and Mario Lemieux for the most through a player's first eight games. Zach Hyman scored on the power play in his first game back, and Mathieu Joseph, Kasperi Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl made it 5-0 before the second period was over. Karel Vejmelka was pulled after five goals on 17 shots, and Sebastian Cossa came in. Tristan Jarry stopped 26 of 28; John Marino and Mikhail Sergachev scored in the third. Trent Frederic and Jack McBain fought. Edmonton is 6-1-1. Utah is 6-3-0, and its three-game win streak just met the one thing in hockey that doesn't care about your streak.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT2VGK6Final: PIT 2, VGK 6

Jack Eichel played his 700th NHL game and celebrated by setting up two goals before Pittsburgh had found its skates. Rasmus Andersson scored at 1:06 and Noah Hanifin at 4:02, both from Eichel and Mark Stone, and Stone added a power-play goal of his own late in the first, finishing with three points. Rookie Trevor Connelly scored on a breakaway, his fourth goal, and now leads all NHL rookies in goals and points. Shea Theodore and Brett Howden, into an empty net, rounded it out. Sidney Crosby scored on the power play and Evgeni Malkin added another, so the two franchise icons did all the scoring while the rest of the roster watched. Adin Hill stopped 22 of 24; Sergei Murashov allowed five on 19. Jeremy Lauzon and Declan Carlile fought early. Vegas is 8-2-0. Pittsburgh is 3-5-1, and Vegas just reminded the Penguins that the house always wins.

Saturday, October 17

Game recap

PIT2COL5Final: PIT 2, COL 5

Pittsburgh got the old band back together for about eight minutes. Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust scored 29 seconds apart in the first period, the Penguins led 2-0 in Denver, and then the Avalanche remembered they're the Avalanche. Artturi Lehkonen scored late in the first and again 25 seconds into the second, Gabriel Landeskog put Colorado ahead, T.J. Hughes scored his first NHL goal, and Nathan MacKinnon closed it on the power play in the third for a 5-2 final. MacKinnon had a goal, three assists and nine shots, Martin Necas added three assists, Cale Makar two, and Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 29 of 31. Arturs Silovs made 27 saves on 32. The Penguins have lost two straight and play in Vegas tonight on a back-to-back. Five unanswered goals: the whole 'retool on the fly' plan, summed up in one evening.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BOS4ANA2Final: BOS 4, ANA 2

Anaheim did all its work in a 21-second burst at the end of the first period: Tim Washe and Beckett Sennecke scored at 19:22 and 19:43, and the Ducks went to the room up 2-0. Then they kept visiting the penalty box, and Boston kept cashing in. Frederic Brunet scored his first NHL goal on the power play in the second, David Pastrnak tied it on the power play early in the third, and Elias Lindholm made it three power-play goals for the lead at 8:18. Matthew Poitras added insurance with 3:40 left for a 4-2 final. James Hagens set up two goals in 10 minutes of ice time, Nikita Zadorov threw six hits and sat for six penalty minutes, and Michael DiPietro stopped 25 of 27 for his first NHL win. Lukas Dostal made 18 saves on 22. Boston went 3-for-4 on the power play and killed all five of Anaheim's. That's four straight wins for the Bruins and two straight losses for the Ducks, whose penalty kill spent the night handing out party favors.

Friday, October 16

Game recap

BUF5TOR4OTFinal: BUF 5, TOR 4 OT

Toronto led 4-2 after 40 minutes in its own building, which, if you've followed this franchise, is not the same thing as winning. Kirill Marchenko scored a hat trick, one on the power play, and Auston Matthews scored 2:24 in, so the Leafs did their part for two periods. Then Buffalo took the third: Dennis Gilbert and Mattias Samuelsson scored 2:11 apart, and Owen Power won it 3:14 into overtime. Jack Quinn had the full evening: two goals, two assists and a second-period fight with Troy Stecher. Neither goalie will frame this one: Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 26 of 30, Sergei Bobrovsky 29 of 34. Gavin McKenna played 6:36 and watched the last 33 minutes from the bench. Toronto is 3-3-2, and blowing a two-goal third-period lead at home to the Sabres is the kind of thing Leafs fans stopped calling a surprise years ago.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI1OTT2SOFinal: NYI 1, OTT 2 SO

Two teams combined for 40 shots and two goals in 65 minutes, so naturally it took a skills competition to settle it. Matias Maccelli gave the Islanders the lead with 12 seconds left in the first, unassisted, and Ridly Greig tied it late in the second with his first of the season. After that, Linus Ullmark (20 saves on 21 shots) and Semyon Varlamov (18 on 19) took turns making everyone else look silly. The first four shooters in the shootout came up empty before Shane Pinto scored in the third round, and Simon Holmstrom missed to end it. The Senators are 6-2 with 12 points. The Islanders are 3-3-1, and their offense went quiet after the first intermission and never came back, like a fan base that's been waiting since 1983.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA3TBL4OTFinal: SEA 3, TBL 4 OT

Seattle came into Tampa on a three-game road win streak and left with a point and a long flight home. Ryan Winterton opened the scoring, Brandon Hagel answered with two goals for the Lightning, and the lead changed hands until Matty Beniers tied it 3-3 with 4:19 left in regulation. Jared McCann had the Kraken's power-play goal in between, and Ilya Mikheyev's unassisted goal had put Tampa back in front. Then Victor Hedman scored his first of the season 2:07 into overtime off a Pontus Holmberg feed, because of course the old man was the one who jumped into the play. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 24 of 27; Philipp Grubauer stopped 31 of 35. The Lightning are 5-2. The Kraken are 5-2-1 and got outshot 35-27, the hockey version of a Florida beach day in October: you still get burned.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2FLA3OTFinal: VAN 2, FLA 3 OT

Vancouver led 2-0 for more than 40 minutes, had Leevi Meriläinen stopping everything, and was 13 seconds from ending its losing streak. Then Brady Tkachuk happened. He cut it to 2-1 at 11:11 of the third, tied it with 13 seconds left and the goalie pulled, and won it 2:23 into overtime off Seth Jones and Sam Reinhart. Natural hat trick, all after the second intermission. Liam Ohgren and Elias Pettersson scored for the Canucks, Pettersson off a feed from Filip Chytil in his season debut. Meriläinen made 36 saves on 39 shots; Akira Schmid needed only 15 on 17 at the other end. Florida is 4-2-2. The Canucks are 2-6-1 with six straight losses, and blowing a two-goal lead with 13 seconds left is how a road trip turns into a support group.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR1NJD7Final: NYR 1, NJD 7

The Rangers walked into Newark at 6-2 and walked out with a 7-1 souvenir. Evan Rodrigues scored with 30 seconds left in the first, and then the second period turned into a fire drill: Luke Hughes, Nico Hischier and Arseny Gritsyuk scored in the first 4:39, and Dylan Garand was pulled after four goals on 13 shots. Spencer Martin came on, and Hughes beat him too for his second of the night. Stefan Noesen and a shorthanded Cody Glass piled on in the third, with Pavel Dorofeyev's power-play goal the Rangers' only reply. Nico Daws stopped 18 of 19. Will Cuylle and Johnathan Kovacevic fought in the first, and Alexis Lafrenière got a misconduct in the third, which at least got him out of the building early. The Devils are 4-3. The Rangers are 6-3, and that shiny goal difference just took a six-goal haircut.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI1DET2Final: PHI 1, DET 2

The Flyers scored first, which at this point is just how they set up the punchline. Matvei Michkov went in alone late in the first, unassisted, and Daniil Tarasov didn't allow anything else on 18 shots. Detroit tied it early in the second when Anton Johansson scored his first of the season, set up by Dylan Larkin, and Andrew Copp won it with 4:38 left, also his first. Joseph Woll was good for Philadelphia, 24 saves on 26 shots, and it bought him nothing. The Red Wings are 2-3-2. The Flyers are 0-6-3 with 11 goals in nine games, and the only thing they've won all season is the race to the bottom of the standings.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG3CHI4OTFinal: WPG 3, CHI 4 OT

Connor Bedard scored his first goal of the season on a first-period power play, and the Blackhawks spent the rest of the night making sure it wasn't wasted. Frank Nazar and Ryan Donato made it 3-1 inside 18 minutes, but Winnipeg chipped back: Neal Pionk scored one and set up two more, Kyle Connor got his eighth on the power play, and Alex Iafallo tied it early in the third. Then Artyom Levshunov, from Bedard and Patrick Kane, scored his first of the season 1:37 into overtime. Spencer Knight stopped 31 of 34; Stuart Skinner stopped 24 of 28. Chicago is 3-5. The Jets are 4-1-2 and got a point, but every night they give up four is another reminder of who isn't in their crease.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS3NSH2SOFinal: SJS 3, NSH 2 SO

San Jose was one second away from its first regulation win of the season. One. Mason Marchment and Will Smith had the Sharks up 2-0 into the third, Ryan O'Reilly got one back on the power play, and Steven Stamkos tied it with the goalie pulled at 19:59. So off to extra time, again, and a shootout, where Macklin Celebrini scored and Alex Nedeljkovic stopped Ryan O'Reilly, Filip Forsberg and Ross Colton. Nedeljkovic made 32 saves on 34 shots, Juuse Saros 30 on 32. Nicolas Hague and Zack Ostapchuk fought 2:51 in. The Sharks are 4-3, and all four wins needed more than 60 minutes. Nashville is 2-2-3: seven games, two wins, and a team that has mastered every part of hockey except the part where you win.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL4MIN5Final: STL 4, MIN 5

Matt Boldy scored a hat trick, and the Wild still spent the last minute hanging on. Jonatan Berggren gave St. Louis a power-play lead 1:45 in, and then Minnesota took over: Boldy on the power play, Danila Yurov, then Boldy, Kirill Kaprizov (his ninth) and Boldy again in the second for a 5-2 lead. Quinn Hughes had two assists. The Blues made it close late: Robert Thomas scored shorthanded with four minutes left, and Dylan Holloway made it 5-4 with 15 seconds left and the goalie pulled. Jesper Wallstedt held on with 21 saves on 25 shots, and Joel Hofer stopped 33 of 38. Minnesota is 5-2-1. St. Louis is 3-3-1 and showed up about 40 minutes late, which is fashionable at a party and fatal in Saint Paul.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA4EDM2Final: UTA 4, EDM 2

Edmonton's five-game win streak ended at home, and Utah did it with special teams. Barrett Hayton and Clayton Keller scored on power plays, Logan Cooley made it 3-1 just 23 seconds after Leon Draisaitl had cut it to 2-1 (from Connor McDavid, naturally), and Keller added an empty-netter with 28 seconds left. Shakir Mukhamadullin had given the Oilers hope early in the third with an extra attacker on. Karel Vejmelka stopped 22 of 24, and Devon Levi stopped 20 of 23. Utah is 6-2 with 12 points. The Oilers are 5-1-1, and a loss in October is fine in Edmonton; it's the ones in June that keep the whole city up at night.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CGY2VGK6Final: CGY 2, VGK 6

Brett Howden scored 25 seconds in, and the Flames spent the rest of the night chasing a game that had already left the building. Jack Eichel added a shorthanded goal, Braeden Bowman scored on the power play, and then Mark Stone took over the third: three goals, the last on the power play, for a hat trick. Ivan Barbashev had three assists, Eichel and Mitch Marner two each. Jake Middleton scored shorthanded and Matt Coronato added a late power-play goal for Calgary. Carter Hart stopped 28 of 30, and Dustin Wolf faced 33 shots and stopped 27. Vegas is 7-2 with 14 points. The Flames are 1-6, and Vegas showed them the kind of hospitality the Strip saves for tourists who bet on the wrong team.

Thursday, October 15

Game recap

MTL4WSH5Final: MTL 4, WSH 5

Nine goals, three ties and one Alex Tuch, who decided Washington's 5-4 win over Montreal was his personal project. Tuch scored shorthanded and unassisted at 6:16 of the second to give the Capitals their first lead, 3-2, then added another unassisted goal at 17:05 of the third for a 5-3 cushion he'd need. Josh Anderson scored twice for Montreal, both set up by Alex Newhook, and Lane Hutson had a goal and an assist, but the Canadiens never led after the first period. Justin Holl, of all people, scored the winner at 12:29 of the third. Nick Suzuki made it interesting with a 6-on-5 power-play goal at 18:21, and that was as close as it got. Charlie Lindgren stopped 26 of 30; Jakub Dobes saw 23 shots and let in five. Montreal falls to 3-3-1, Washington climbs to 4-3. Two straight shootout wins had the Habs feeling clutch; turns out you can't buy a skills competition in regulation.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL3COL2SOFinal: DAL 3, COL 2 SO

Colorado won the first half of this back-to-back 3-2 in Dallas on Tuesday. Dallas flew to Denver and returned the exact score, plus a shootout, for the full refund. Gabriel Landeskog opened it in the second off a Nazem Kadri feed, Miro Heiskanen answered late in the period in a 30-minute shift at the office, and Arttu Hyry scored shorthanded 1:20 into the third for his first of the season. Brock Nelson tied it at 8:21 and that was the last anybody would score with a goalie in the way. In the shootout, Jason Robertson and Roope Hintz beat Scott Wedgewood, Kadri answered once, and Nathan MacKinnon, Martin Necas and Nelson all came up empty. Casey DeSmith stopped 25 of 27, Wedgewood 20 of 22. Dallas gets to 3-3-1; Colorado is 4-2-1. Cale Makar came back for this one, and the Avs still went 1-for-4 against Casey DeSmith in the shootout, which is a sentence that should cost somebody dessert.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Wednesday, October 14

Game recap

NJD5DET4OTFinal: NJD 5, DET 4 OT

The Devils and Red Wings spent the night trading goals like neither team had heard of defense, and Jack Hughes ended it 1:19 into overtime, 5-4 New Jersey. Jesper Bratt set up the winner and finished with a goal and two assists, while Hughes had a goal, two helpers and eight shots. Detroit led 2-1 early in the second on Michael Brandsegg-Nygård's goal, then New Jersey went ahead twice, on a Nico Hischier power-play goal and a Bratt snipe, and Alex DeBrincat tied it both times. His second, at 5:46 of the third, gave him two goals and an assist. Neither goalie will be framing this one. Jake Allen stopped 23 of 27 and John Gibson 32 of 37. The Devils are 3-3-0. Detroit is 1-3-2 and took home the loser point, which at this rate is the franchise's main export.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA7CBJ3Final: FLA 7, CBJ 3

Brady Tkachuk spent the night proving the family business is a good one. He scored a hat trick, two of them on the power play, and his brother Matthew assisted on Florida's first five goals as the Panthers buried Columbus 7-3. Kent Johnson gave the Blue Jackets a 1-0 lead in the first, which turned out to be the high point of their evening. Florida then scored six straight, four on the power play, with Carter Verhaeghe scoring twice and Sam Reinhart adding two of his own, the last into an empty net. Seth Jones had four assists. Cam Talbot stopped 17 of 23 before Jet Greaves came on and stopped all four he saw, and Akira Schmid made 24 saves on 27. The Panthers are 3-2-2. Columbus is 2-3-0, and its penalty kill should be charged as an accomplice.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF3MTL4SOFinal: BUF 3, MTL 4 SO

Montreal outshot Buffalo 38-17 and still needed a shootout, which tells you everything about Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen's night. He stopped 35 of 38, and the Canadiens won 4-3 anyway when Cole Caufield, Alexandre Texier and Zachary Bolduc went three for three in the skills competition. Lane Hutson scored on the power play and set up Josh Anderson, Caufield had a goal and an assist, and the Habs led 3-1 through two. Then Buffalo woke up for 61 seconds, with Josh Norris scoring at 4:24 of the third and Olen Zellweger getting his second of the night at 5:25. Jacob Fowler made 14 saves on 17. Tage Thompson scored in the shootout and Jack Quinn did not. Montreal is 3-2-1. The Sabres are 3-3-1 and managed 17 shots in 65 minutes, which is less a game plan than a dare.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH2CAR4Final: WSH 2, CAR 4

Washington led twice and Carolina never looked worried about it. Andrei Svechnikov scored twice, the second a power-play goal at 13:56 of the third that broke a 2-2 tie, then set up Mark Jankowski's empty-netter as the Hurricanes won 4-2. Boone Jenner and, of all people, Justin Holl gave the Capitals their leads. Svechnikov answered the first and Eric Robinson tied it late in the second. Carolina outshot Washington 35-22, and Logan Thompson kept it close with 31 saves on 34, while Pyotr Kochetkov needed only 20 saves on 22. The Hurricanes are 6-1-1 and look exactly like the Hurricanes. The Capitals are 3-3-0, and their plan of hanging around until Carolina gets bored has a long history of not working.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SEA3PHI2SOFinal: SEA 3, PHI 2 SO

The Flyers finally found a third period they liked and still couldn't win. Down 2-0 on goals from Bobby McMann, on the power play, and Ville Ottavainen, Philadelphia tied it in 73 seconds early in the third. Christian Dvorak scored with Dan Vladar picking up an assist, then Trevor Zegras evened it. Vladar was the best Flyer in the building, stopping 29 of 31 and setting up a goal. In the shootout Matty Beniers and Matvei Michkov traded goals, and McMann ended it in the fifth round for a 3-2 Seattle win. Philipp Grubauer made 24 saves on 26. The Kraken are 5-2-0. The Flyers are 0-5-3, eight games without a win, and the loser points are piling up like participation ribbons.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL1NYR4Final: TBL 1, NYR 4

Alexis Lafrenière scored twice before Tampa Bay had found its legs, at 1:02 and 12:47 of the first, both set up by Tye Kartye, and the Rangers beat the Lightning 4-1. Zemgus Girgensons got one back late in the first, and that was all Dylan Garand allowed, 25 saves on 26. Will Cuylle scored late in the second and threw 11 hits, which reads less like a stat line than a demolition permit. Mika Zibanejad closed it with a shorthanded empty-netter. Matt Rempe and Jeffrey Viel fought in the first, because Rempe was dressed. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 19 of 22. New York is 6-2-0. Tampa is 4-2-0, and Kucherov, Point, Hagel and Guentzel combined for zero points, which the Lightning would like filed under clerical error.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL7OTT2Final: STL 7, OTT 2

Ottawa came in 5-1-0 and feeling good about itself. St. Louis fixed that, 7-2 at Canadian Tire Centre. Pius Suter opened the scoring shorthanded in the first and added another, Mason McTavish scored twice including a power-play goal, Jake Neighbours had two, and Adam Jiricek scored his first of the season to make it 7-1. Pavel Buchnevich had three assists, and the Blues scored four times in the third. Samuel Ersson faced 26 shots and stopped 19, while Joel Hofer stopped 15 of 17. Claude Giroux and Fabian Zetterlund, on the power play, scored for Ottawa, which managed 17 shots all night. Dylan Peterson and Jorian Donovan fought in the third, the closest the Senators came to winning anything. St. Louis is 3-2-1. Ottawa is 5-2-0, and its defense spent the night as decorative trim.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2NYI3Final: VAN 2, NYI 3

Vancouver dressed two Elias Petterssons and still came up a goal short. Kyle Palmieri scored twice for the Islanders, including the winner at 5:38 of the third off a Matias Maccelli feed, and New York won 3-2. Maccelli also scored in the first, 53 seconds after Palmieri's opener, and Matthew Schaefer had two assists. The Canucks clawed back on goals from Max Sasson and Brock Boeser, Boeser's on the power play late in the second, but the Islanders outshot them 38-26. Leevi Meriläinen made 35 saves on 38 to keep it close, and Ilya Sorokin stopped 24 of 26. The Islanders are 3-3-0. The Canucks are 2-6-0, and right now the only race they're leading is the one to the draft lottery.

Game recap

PIT3CHI5Final: PIT 3, CHI 5

Sidney Crosby dragged Pittsburgh back from two goals down, and Chicago still won, 5-3. Teuvo Teravainen opened the scoring 28 seconds in and ended up with two goals and an assist, including the winner at 15:42 of the third, about six minutes after Crosby's second goal had tied it 3-3. Roman Kantserov scored twice, one on the power play from Connor Bedard, and Anton Frondell picked up two assists. Tyler Bertuzzi added the empty-netter with 10 seconds left. Spencer Knight stopped 24 of 27, while Sergei Murashov made 15 saves on 19 shots, which is a lot of goals for a team that only managed 20 shots. The Blackhawks get their second win and sit 2-5-0. The Penguins are 3-3-1, and losing to a team that came in with one win is a tough way to waste two Crosby goals.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN2WPG5Final: MIN 2, WPG 5

Kirill Kaprizov scored twice in the first period in Winnipeg, and Minnesota never scored again. The Jets won 5-2. Cole Perfetti scored 1:50 in and later broke the 2-2 tie on a power play at 16:36 of the second. Mark Scheifele had a goal and two assists, Kyle Connor scored unassisted early in the third, and Cole Koepke finished it. Neal Pionk had two assists. Stuart Skinner stopped 19 of 21, and Calvin Pickard made 20 saves on 25 shots. Quinn Hughes logged 28:25 and got one assist. Winnipeg is 4-1-1 and Minnesota is 4-2-1, both with 9 points. The Wild got outscored 3-0 over the last 40 minutes, and once Kaprizov stopped scoring, so did everybody else.

Game recap

COL3DAL2Final: COL 3, DAL 2

Colorado won 3-2 in Dallas in a game that had more fights than Stars goals in the second period. Nathan MacKinnon set up two goals and dropped the gloves with Roope Hintz, and Fedor Svechkov fought Radek Faksa and racked up 17 penalty minutes in 11:24 of ice time. Martin Necas scored twice, the second on the power play at 16:14 of the second, and that one held up as the winner. Artturi Lehkonen opened the scoring. For Dallas, Tyler Seguin had a power-play goal, an assist and seven shots, and Hintz scored early in the third to make it close. Mackenzie Blackwood stopped 24 of 26, and Jake Oettinger made 22 saves on 25. The Avalanche are 4-2-0. The Stars are 2-3-1, and Hintz was the only Star willing to get in MacKinnon's way all night.

Game recap

VGK5NSH2Final: VGK 5, NSH 2

Five Vegas players scored in a 5-2 win in Nashville, so blaming one guy won't help the Predators. Ryan O'Reilly scored first, then Tomas Hertl and Jack Eichel answered before the first period ended. Adam Edstrom tied it 2-2 with a shorthanded goal in the second, and William Karlsson put Vegas back ahead with 2:16 left in the period. Trevor Connelly and Brett Howden then scored 95 seconds apart early in the third. Howden had a goal and an assist, and Rasmus Andersson had two assists. Adin Hill stopped 25 of 27, and Juuse Saros made 20 saves on 25 shots. Filip Forsberg had seven shots and one assist. The Golden Knights are 6-2-0. Nashville is 2-2-2 and outshot Vegas 27-25, which counts for exactly nothing in the standings.

Game recap

TOR4UTA5Final: TOR 4, UTA 5

Utah scored five times in the first 40 minutes and then hung on to beat Toronto 5-4. Daniil But, Vincent Trocheck, Mikhail Sergachev, Dylan Guenther and MacKenzie Weegar all scored for the Mammoth, and Sergachev's came shorthanded. Auston Matthews scored on the power play and had an assist, John Tavares had a power-play goal and an assist, and Gavin McKenna made it 5-4 with Anthony Stolarz pulled at 11:01 of the third. The Leafs got no closer. Stolarz stopped 23 of 28, and Karel Vejmelka made 22 saves on 26. Utah is 5-2-0. Toronto is 3-3-1, and digging a 3-0 hole in 25 minutes is a strange way to make a game interesting.

Game recap

CGY4ANA2Final: CGY 4, ANA 2

Calgary finally won a game, 4-2 in Anaheim, and the Flames had to come from behind to do it. Adam Klapka scored first, but Beckett Sennecke and Leo Carlsson, on the power play, put the Ducks ahead in the first period. Aydar Suniev tied it in the second, and Martin Pospisil scored the winner at 15:38 of the third, his first goal of the season, with an assist from Suniev. Yegor Sharangovich added the empty-netter. Klapka also fought Jeff Malott. Dustin Wolf stopped 23 of 25, and Lukas Dostal made 32 saves on 35 while Calgary outshot Anaheim 36-25. The Flames are 1-5-0. The Ducks are 4-2-0, and they gave up 36 shots to a team that came in without a win, which is how you end up somebody's highlight of the season.

Devon Levi stopped 39 of 40 shots, and Edmonton beat Los Angeles 4-1 on 17 shots of its own. Connor McDavid had a goal and three assists, and the Oilers scored three times in the first period. Anton Forsberg stopped all nine shots he faced after coming in. Brandt Clarke scored late in the second for the Kings, and Podkolzin's empty-netter, his second goal, closed it out. Edmonton is 5-0-1. The Kings are 0-3-2, have yet to win, and needed 40 shots to score one goal.

Tuesday, October 13

Game recap

FLA3BUF5Final: FLA 3, BUF 5

Both starting goalies got the hook in Buffalo, and the Sabres won anyway, 5-3. Colten Ellis lasted nine shots before Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen took over and stopped 13 of 14 for the win, while Jacob Markstrom left after 11 shots and Akira Schmid finished with 18 saves on 21. Josh Doan opened the scoring, Rasmus Dahlin scored on the power play and Ryan McLeod put Buffalo ahead again, but Sam Reinhart tied it twice with power-play goals. Then Florida kept taking penalties, five in all, and Noah Ostlund scored on the power play at 7:15 of the third. Tage Thompson added the insurance goal six minutes later. Buffalo outshot Florida 32-23 and gets back to .500 at 3-3. The Panthers are 2-2-2, have lost two straight, and play again tonight in Columbus. Two of their three goals came on the power play, and without Barkov their even-strength offense is mostly a rumor.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT4NJD1Final: OTT 4, NJD 1

Linus Ullmark is 5-0, and the Senators are starting to act like a team that expects this. He stopped 29 of 30 in New Jersey, joining Ray Emery and Dominik Hasek as the only Ottawa goalies to win their first five or more starts of a season. Shane Pinto scored nine seconds into the second period, before half the building had found its seat again. Stephen Halliday added a power-play goal, and Tim Stutzle got his fifth of the year plus an assist. Arseny Gritsyuk broke the shutout with 5:01 left, and Tyler Kleven ended it with an empty-netter. The Devils outshot Ottawa 30-20 and still lost by three, and Nicolas Daws stopped 16 of 19. Anthony Mantha also took a five-minute boarding major in the first. Ottawa has won three straight and is 5-1. New Jersey is 2-3 and has given up the first goal in all five of its games, which is the kind of consistency nobody asked for.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK2MIN4Final: VGK 2, MIN 4

Minnesota was up 3-0 after 20 minutes and spent the rest of the night guarding the lead, a 4-2 win that ended Vegas's four-game winning streak. Matt Boldy, Maxim Shabanov (on the power play) and Danila Yurov all scored in a 5:07 stretch of the first period, and Quinn Hughes set up the first two. Rasmus Andersson and William Karlsson pulled Vegas within one, but Joel Eriksson Ek's empty-netter settled it with 1:22 left. Jesper Wallstedt made 21 saves on 23 shots. Rookie Rieger Lorenz picked up his first NHL point and dropped the gloves with Jeremy Lauzon, which is quite a first week. The Wild killed all five Vegas power plays, so their penalty kill is 21 for 22, and their power play has scored in all six games. Minnesota is 4-1-1. Vegas is 5-2 and found out that winning one-goal games works better when you score the first goal.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Monday, October 12

Game recap

SEA5WSH3Final: SEA 5, WSH 3

Washington spent Sunday chasing Seattle and kept catching it, which turned out to be the problem: every time the Caps tied it, the Kraken just scored again. Kaapo Kakko opened it, Jordan Kyrou and Alex Ovechkin answered for a 2-1 Caps lead, and Jordan Eberle tied it with 11 seconds left in the first. Ovi's first of the season came against the 190th different goalie he's beaten, a record, which is a lot of goaltending careers to have ruined. Frederick Gaudreau put Seattle back in front, Boone Jenner tied it 46 seconds into the third, and then Jared McCann won it with 5:27 left before Ryan Winterton iced it. Gaudreau, Winterton and Ben Meyers built two goals together and left with two points each. Joey Daccord stopped 33 of 36; Logan Thompson 22 of 27. Jakob Chychrun fired eight shots and scored none, which sums up a Capitals night with all the volume of a farewell tour and none of the encore.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2NYR6Final: VAN 2, NYR 6

Vancouver showed up at Madison Square Garden on the second night of a back-to-back and played like it had already checked out of the hotel. Tye Kartye scored 27 seconds in, and he and Will Cuylle both finished with two goals, which is not the scoring forecast anybody printed in September. The Canucks did hang around: Jake DeBrusk tied it in the first, and Elias Pettersson (the defenseman; Vancouver carries two of them, just in case) tied it 2-2 shorthanded late in the second. Kartye answered 89 seconds later, and the third was a parade: Alexis Lafrenière on the power play for his fifth, Gabe Perreault, then Cuylle again. J.T. Miller had two assists against his old team and Mika Zibanejad two more. Dylan Garand made 19 saves in his first start since Shesterkin was ruled out for the season; Kevin Lankinen allowed six on 25. That's four straight losses for the Canucks, and a six-game road trip is a long time to be this bad in public.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR4PHI1Final: CAR 4, PHI 1

Philadelphia is now 0-5-2, the worst start in franchise history, and Carolina made sure the Flyers set the record in front of the home crowd. After a scoreless first, the Canes scored three times in 6:38 of the second: Andrei Svechnikov, then former Flyer Shayne Gostisbehere, then Sebastian Aho right after Christian Dvorak had briefly made it 2-1. Mark Jankowski added one in the third. William Carrier had two assists, and Pyotr Kochetkov stopped 18 of 19, which was about all the work Philly's 19 shots asked of him. Joseph Woll made 26 saves on 30. Carolina has won five straight, and did it Sunday without captain Jordan Staal. The Flyers have eight goals in seven games, and by the third period some fans were chanting for Rick Tocchet's job. Philadelphia hasn't won a game yet, but the building already has a playoff atmosphere: loud, angry and aimed at the bench.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Sunday, October 11

Game recap

PHI1BOS5Final: PHI 1, BOS 5

The Flyers came to Boston looking for their first win and left with another lesson in what a real NHL team looks like. Boston won 5-1, and Fraser Minten ran the show with a goal and two assists. Pavel Zacha opened the scoring in the first off a David Pastrnak feed, and Mason Lohrei made it 2-0 late in the second. In the third the Bruins piled on with goals from Marat Khusnutdinov, Casey Mittelstadt and Minten. Philadelphia's lone highlight was Porter Martone's power-play goal at 6:32 of the third, which counted for exactly nothing. Jeremy Swayman had a nap with 14 saves on 15 shots. Dan Vladar faced 32 shots and made 27 saves, mostly because no Flyer stood in front of anything. Philly is still winless, and the Broad Street Bullies are now just Broad Street.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN1NJD4Final: VAN 1, NJD 4

Jake Allen started his 500th NHL game and stopped 20 of 21 shots as New Jersey beat Vancouver 4-1. The Canucks were feeling good for about eight minutes after Linus Karlsson's power-play goal. Then Nico Hischier tied it on a Devils power play, Jesper Boqvist put them ahead late in the first, and Jesper Bratt and Hischier added two more power-play goals in the second. Hischier's second came with ten seconds left in the period, which is a Vancouver penalty kill in a nutshell. Jack Hughes set up both second-period goals. Leevi Merilainen made 31 saves on 34 shots, and when his skate blade came out twice, Kevin Lankinen got 5:27 of emergency cameo work. Three of New Jersey's four goals came on the power play. The Canucks' PK keeps auditioning for a job as the other team's best player.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM3SJS1Final: EDM 3, SJS 1

Edmonton won 3-1 in San Jose with goals from three guys you'd never put on a jersey order. Mattias Ekholm scored the only goal of the first 43 minutes. Vasily Podkolzin, set up by Connor McDavid, made it 2-0 early in the third with his fifth goal, which is already a pace that makes Oilers fans nervous. Alex Formenton added another 2:27 later. Macklin Celebrini spoiled Tristan Jarry's shutout with 8:41 left, and Jarry finished with 19 saves on 20 shots. Yaroslav Askarov stopped 17 of 20 and deserved better than the 20 shots his team managed at the other end. The Sharks got outshot, outscored and out-depth-charted by the Oilers' bottom six. San Jose's rebuild is past the teardown stage and still waiting on a building permit.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN4FLA1Final: MIN 4, FLA 1

Florida threw a home opener and Kirill Kaprizov took over the party, scoring his seventh career hat trick as Minnesota won 4-1. Matt Boldy scored 53 seconds in, before the banner-night buzz had worn off. Kaprizov added a power-play goal at 6:18, and Michael McCarron and Bokondji Imama fought soon after, the most Florida pushback all night. Matthew Tkachuk scored unassisted early in the second to cut it to 2-1. Kaprizov answered less than three minutes later, then finished the hat trick into an empty net with 1:04 left, in the Panthers' own building. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 29 of 30 shots. Jacob Markstrom made 25 saves on 28. Hard to defend the Cup city when you can't defend one guy.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA4BUF1Final: UTA 4, BUF 1

Tage Thompson scored on the power play eight minutes in, and Buffalo's lead lasted 2:12. Then Utah reeled off four straight goals and won 4-1 at KeyBank Center. Kailer Yamamoto tied it, Nick Schmaltz scored his sixth goal on a power play late in the second, and Anders Lee added another 2:01 later. John Marino finished it on the power play early in the third. Barrett Hayton had two assists, and Karel Vejmelka was barely bothered, stopping 23 of 24. Colten Ellis made 26 saves on 30 shots. MacKenzie Weegar and Peyton Krebs fought at the end of the second, which was the only time a Sabre won a puck battle all night. Buffalo's playoff drought now has its own season-ticket package.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET0MTL1SOFinal: DET 0, MTL 1 SO

Sixty-five minutes, 60 shots and zero goals, and Montreal won 1-0 in a shootout. Jacob Fowler started his second straight game for the Habs and stopped all 30 shots. Daniil Tarasov did the same at the other end, 30 saves on 30 shots, and got nothing for it. The shootout went six rounds of misses (Caufield, Suzuki, Hutson, Raymond, DeBrincat, Larkin) before Zachary Bolduc beat Tarasov. Nate Danielson then missed, and the night was over. One team had a 23-year-old goalie and a reason to celebrate. The other had Dylan Larkin, Alex DeBrincat and Lucas Raymond and couldn't buy one goal in 65 minutes or six attempts. Detroit's offense has the scoring touch of a Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH2OTT3SOFinal: NSH 2, OTT 3 SO

Matt Murray made his first NHL start since January 2024, and Nashville led 2-0 in Ottawa for most of the night before losing 3-2 in a shootout. Ross Colton scored first and Jonathan Marchessault added a power-play goal in the first. Tim Stützle cut it in half on a second-period power play. With Linus Ullmark pulled, Drake Batherson tied it at 18:37 of the third. Ryan O'Reilly scored in the shootout's first round, but Stützle and Shane Pinto answered, and Steven Stamkos missed to end it. Murray stopped 18 of 20 shots and Ullmark stopped 16 of 18. The Preds held a two-goal lead until the final 83 seconds and lost anyway. Nashville protects a lead like it protected its last few playoff hopes.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL1PIT2SOFinal: DAL 1, PIT 2 SO

Forty-five shots, two goals in 65 minutes and a skills competition to settle it: Pittsburgh beat Dallas 2-1 in a shootout. Connor Dewar broke the deadlock 1:57 into the third off a Blake Lizotte feed, so the fourth line did what the stars wouldn't. Then Tyler Seguin, with Jake Oettinger pulled for the extra attacker, tied it with 30 seconds left. It was his first goal since November's ACL injury. Arturs Silovs stopped 24 of 25 and Oettinger made 19 saves on 20, so the goalies earned their pay. In the shootout, Ben Kindel, Sidney Crosby and Rickard Rakell all scored, Seguin and Wyatt Johnston answered, and Mikko Rantanen's miss in the fourth round ended it. Radek Faksa left with a lower-body injury. Dallas outshot Pittsburgh 25-20 and still lost, which is very Stars: always close, from conference finals to breakaway contests.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR5CHI2Final: CAR 5, CHI 2

Carolina went into Chicago and won 5-2, and the Blackhawks were lucky it was only three. Mark Jankowski scored with 57 seconds left in the first. Early in the second, the Canes scored three goals in under four minutes. Sebastian Aho scored shorthanded for the second straight game, which is great for him and awkward for a Chicago power play that keeps handing the puck to the other team. Jackson Blake added his first of the season, and after Roman Kantserov's solo goal briefly got the United Center up, Taylor Hall made it 4-1. Jordan Martinook added a fifth in the third, and Oliver Moore got one back late. Mike Reilly had two assists, Carolina outshot Chicago 39-26, and Spencer Knight stopped 34 of 39 while getting no help. Brandon Bussi made 24 saves on 26. Chicago's rebuild has reached the stage where it gets beaten by the other team's penalty killers.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CBJ3STL5Final: CBJ 3, STL 5

Columbus led St. Louis 2-0 after one period and lost 5-3. Being good for 20 minutes is something the Blue Jackets have mastered. Valeri Nichushkin opened the scoring, and Kent Johnson made it 2-0 with 12 seconds left in the first. Ross Johnston and Mathieu Olivier fought 21 seconds into the second, and the Blues took over from there. Jake Neighbours scored, then Jimmy Snuggerud scored twice in 3:30, and Dylan Holloway set up all three goals for a three-assist night. Cole Sillinger tied it 3-3 midway through the third. Less than three minutes later, Jonatan Berggren scored with the extra attacker on to put St. Louis ahead, and Pavel Buchnevich added an empty-netter. Jordan Binnington stopped 20 of 23, and Jet Greaves made 22 saves on 26. Columbus turned a two-goal lead into a two-goal loss in about 40 minutes, which is quick work even by its standards.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR6COL3Final: TOR 6, COL 3

William Nylander had five points and reached 700 for his career as Toronto won 6-3 in Denver. Nathan MacKinnon was very good, and the Leafs were better. Nick Blankenburg scored first, then MacKinnon scored twice in the first period on eight shots and put Colorado up 2-1. Nylander tied it on the power play, Brock Nelson put Colorado back ahead, and Nylander tied it again. Then Easton Cowan scored 46 seconds later for a lead Toronto never gave back. Auston Matthews finished with two goals and two assists, a power-play goal and an empty-netter. Sergei Bobrovsky made 30 saves on 33 shots for his first win as a Leaf. Mackenzie Blackwood allowed five goals on 22 shots. Colorado outshot Toronto 33-23 and lost by three at home. That takes a special kind of goaltending, and the Avalanche keep finding it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL5NYI3Final: TBL 5, NYI 3

Brandon Hagel scored a hat trick and the winner as Tampa Bay won 5-3 on Long Island. The Islanders had already spent the night climbing back from 2-0 and 3-1 deficits. Jake Guentzel scored twice for the Lightning, once at even strength and once on the power play. Tony DeAngelo and Jean-Gabriel Pageau got New York back within one, and Brayden Schenn tied it 3-3 on the power play with seven seconds left in the second. The third period was scoreless until Hagel's go-ahead goal with 1:44 left, and 21 seconds later his empty-netter completed the hat trick. Nikita Kucherov had two assists. Andrei Vasilevskiy stopped 20 of 23, and Ilya Sorokin made 21 saves on 25. Matthew Schaefer had eight shots in 27 minutes, and Scott Sabourin and Logan Stanley fought. The Islanders tied it twice and then left the slot open for the winner.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA4CGY2Final: ANA 4, CGY 2

Anaheim won 4-2 in Calgary, and the Flames are 0-5 for the first time in franchise history. They're the only team without a point and have been outscored 27-8. Jackson LaCombe opened the scoring on the power play, Morgan Frost tied it, and Frank Vatrano put the Ducks back in front 45 seconds before the first intermission. Aydar Suniev scored his first NHL goal late in the second to tie it 2-2, which was the high point of Calgary's season so far. Then Ryan Poehling scored the shorthanded winner 5:35 into the third, because the Flames' power play hasn't hurt anyone except the Flames. Nikita Nesterenko added insurance, and Mikael Granlund had two assists. Ville Husso stopped 27 of 29, and Dustin Wolf made 24 saves on 28. Cutter Gauthier left early with an upper-body injury. Calgary's new arena should open before its first point arrives.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

LAK1VGK2OTFinal: LAK 1, VGK 2 OT

Every goal came on the power play, including Mitch Marner's in overtime, as Vegas beat Los Angeles 2-1. The Kings put themselves on the wrong side of special teams again. Trevor Connelly scored 2:37 into the second on the power play, and Artemi Panarin answered with a power-play goal less than four minutes later. Then the goalies took over. Carter Hart stopped 26 of 27 and Darcy Kuemper made 30 saves on 32, enough to get the Kings a point. Scott Laughton and Nic Dowd fought in the second. Overtime ended at 2:40 with Marner scoring on the power play, set up by Mark Stone and Connelly, who each had two points. Stone had both assists on the winner. Los Angeles hung around, kept it close and still found a way to lose, the same thing it did in four straight first-round series against Edmonton.

Saturday, October 10

Game recap

SEA6DET3Final: SEA 6, DET 3

Detroit outshot Seattle 40-24 at home and lost 6-3, which is about the most Red Wings sentence you can write right now. The Wings even led twice: 1-0 on Viktor Arvidsson's power-play goal and 2-1 on William Wallinder's first NHL goal. Then the second period showed up. Seattle scored four straight in under ten minutes, two from Frederick Gaudreau with Mackie Samoskevich and Ben Meyers in between, and John Gibson was done after 34 minutes and 10 saves on 15 shots. Daniil Tarasov made his Red Wings debut in relief (8 of 9). Meyers finished with a goal and two assists, Berkly Catton a goal and an assist, Brandon Montour two helpers, and Philipp Grubauer stopped 37. Vince Dunn added a power-play goal and Michael Brandsegg-Nygård scored his first NHL goal late. Forty shots and three goals: Detroit's offense works about as well as its PR department this month.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYR1WSH3Final: NYR 1, WSH 3

The Rangers scored first and then spent 50 minutes finding out what Logan Thompson looks like on a good night. Alexis Lafrenière's power-play goal in the first, his fourth already, held until the second, when Timothy Liljegren tied it and Boone Jenner went in alone at 17:38 to put Washington ahead for good. Tom Wilson's empty-netter with one second left made it 3-1. Thompson stopped 21 of 22. Igor Shesterkin left after 28 minutes (13 saves on 14 shots) and Dylan Garand finished it, 11 of 12, so New York's goaltending held up fine. The rest of the lineup put 22 shots on net in 60 minutes. The Rangers' power play scored once; the other 58 minutes looked like a team waiting for a cab on Seventh Avenue in the rain.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PIT2CBJ3SOFinal: PIT 2, CBJ 3 SO

Columbus outshot Pittsburgh 45-22 and still needed a shootout, because Sergei Murashov decided he'd be the whole Penguins team. Damon Severson, in his season debut, scored the opener and set up Mathieu Olivier for 2-0 in the second, Cole Sillinger assisting on both. Then the Penguins remembered they employ Bryan Rust and Evgeni Malkin: Rust got one back in the second and Malkin tied it 3:19 into the third, his third of the year. Murashov made 43 saves through 65 minutes. Cam Talbot, in his Blue Jackets debut, needed only 20 on 22 shots. The shootout lasted one goal: Kent Johnson scored in the first round, and Rickard Rakell, Egor Chinakhov and Ben Kindel all missed. Pittsburgh got outshot two to one and left with a point, the hockey version of leaving the casino up five bucks after losing your car.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

ANA5WPG1Final: ANA 5, WPG 1

Anaheim walked into Winnipeg and won 5-1 with goals from guys the Jets' scouting report probably listed as "also dressed." Judd Caulfield opened it late in the first, Tim Washe made it 2-0 in the second, and Jeff Malott set up both. Sam Colangelo made it 3-0 early in the third before Kyle Connor, already at six goals, got Winnipeg on the board. Mikael Granlund answered three and a half minutes later, and Nikita Nesterenko added the empty-netter. Lukas Dostal stopped 15 of 16. Clay Stevenson made 12 saves on 16 shots at the other end. Travis Mitchell and Adam Lowry dropped the gloves at the end of the first, the most pushback Winnipeg offered all night. Sixteen shots on goal at home: the Jets' offense is about as easy to find as Connor Hellebuyck this month.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Friday, October 9

Game recap

UTA1BOS6Final: UTA 1, BOS 6

Utah outshot Boston 37-22 and lost by five, which is like winning the argument and getting dumped anyway. The Bruins scored three in the first, Mittelstadt, Pastrnak on the power play and Lohrei, and Sebastian Cossa was on the bench after five saves on eight shots. Karel Vejmelka didn't stop the bleeding: Pastrnak and Geekie scored on the power play early in the second, and Matthew Poitras, the kid Friedman says Edmonton asked about, made it 6-0. Pastrnak finished with two goals and two assists, Geekie a goal and two helpers, and Boston scored three times on the man advantage. Jeremy Swayman stopped 36 of 37 and lost the shutout to Jack McBain midway through the third. Utah's penalty kill spent the night holding the door open, and the Mammoth's shot total will look great on a poster nobody buys.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DAL4BUF0Final: DAL 4, BUF 0

Dallas needed only 18 shots to score four in Buffalo, and the Sabres made every one of them feel like a bargain. Jason Robertson opened it in the first, then the Stars put it away in a six-minute stretch of the second: Sam Steel, Mikko Rantanen and Roope Hintz on the power play. Rantanen had a goal and three assists, Wyatt Johnston three helpers, and the top of the lineup finally looked like the team that was supposed to show up in week one. Jake Oettinger stopped all 26 shots for the shutout. Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen made 14 saves on 18, and Tage Thompson fired six shots with nothing to show for it. Buffalo outshot Dallas and still never scored, which is a pretty good summary of the last decade and a half of Sabres hockey: plenty of effort, no playoff tickets printed.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH5MTL2Final: NSH 5, MTL 2

Montreal led 2-0 midway through the second, outshot Nashville 34-20, and lost by three. Nick Suzuki scored unassisted and Alex Newhook added one from Josh Anderson, and the Bell Centre was warming up the party. Then Alexander Kerfoot got the Predators on the board and Matthew Wood tied it on the power play with 32 seconds left in the second. Ryan O'Reilly won it on another power play with 3:16 to go, and Adam Edstrom scored two empty-netters 71 seconds apart, his only two goals of the season, both into a vacant cage. Roman Josi and Steven Stamkos had two assists each, and Juuse Saros made 32 saves. Jacob Fowler stopped 15 of 18, and Arber Xhekaj logged 10 penalty minutes on a night Nashville scored twice on the power play. The Habs built a two-goal lead and then handed it back like a rental car with an empty tank.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

PHI1OTT2Final: PHI 1, OTT 2

Philadelphia played a tight, tidy road game in Ottawa and lost it anyway, which is now a Flyers tradition five games long. Nick Cousins gave the Senators the lead in the first, Matvei Michkov tied it on a second-period power play from Trevor Zegras and Travis Konecny, and the game sat at 1-1 until Carter Yakemchuk's power-play goal with just under seven minutes left. Claude Giroux had an assist on the winner, back to haunt his old team for a few more minutes. Linus Ullmark stopped 28 of 29 and never looked bothered. Joseph Woll made 24 saves on 26 for Philly and deserved more company on the scoresheet. The Flyers are 0-3-2 and have found every way there is not to win: blowouts, overtimes, and now the classic one-goal special. At this rate the Broad Street Bullies are going to need a Broad Street rebrand.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN2TBL3Final: MIN 2, TBL 3

Tampa scored twice in 36 seconds early in the first and spent the rest of the night guarding the lead like a beach parking spot in July. Anthony Cirelli opened it at 5:26, and John Carlson, wearing the wrong shade of blue for anyone who still has Capitals muscle memory, made it 2-0 at 6:02. Quinn Hughes answered for Minnesota early in the second; Carlson got that one back on the power play off Nikita Kucherov, his second goal on a night he put nine shots on net. Blake Coleman's power-play goal cut it to 3-2 at 14:01 of the second, and that's where it stayed: Dennis Hildeby stopped 34 of 36 and shut the door for the last 26 minutes. Hughes played 32:36, with a goal and an assist, which is a lot of hockey to end with an empty feeling. Jesper Wallstedt made 32 saves in the loss. The Wild outshot Tampa and still went home with nothing, a Minnesota specialty that's lasted longer than most of their playoff runs.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VAN2CAR7Final: VAN 2, CAR 7

Vancouver flew all the way to Raleigh to serve as a power-play clinic. K'Andre Miller scored 78 seconds in, Andrei Svechnikov added two power-play goals before the first was half over, and it was 4-0 when Mark Jankowski scored early in the second. Logan Stankoven then took over: a shorthanded goal, a power-play goal 58 seconds before the second intermission, and the hat trick in the third, all three with Sean Walker getting an assist. Carolina scored four goals with somebody in the box, three on its own power play and one on Vancouver's. Kevin Lankinen allowed six on 18 shots and gave way to Leevi Meriläinen for the third, who stopped 15 of 16. Jake DeBrusk scored both Canucks goals, and Pyotr Kochetkov made 18 saves. The Canucks' penalty kill has the structural integrity of a wet napkin, and Carolina noticed.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CHI1NYI4Final: CHI 1, NYI 4

The Islanders did just enough on Long Island, and Chicago did just enough to make sure it wasn't close. Bo Horvat scored on the power play with 59 seconds left in the first off rookie Matthew Schaefer, and Emil Heineman and Anthony Duclair made it 3-0 in the second. Ilya Sorokin stopped 22 of 23 and only lost the shutout when Frank Nazar scored with Arvid Soderblom pulled at 17:26 of the third, with Patrick Kane on the assist. Horvat hit the empty net 61 seconds later for his second of the night. Nazar's night ended with a match penalty for an illegal check to Horvat's head, and the Sun-Times reports the league could take a look. Soderblom made 15 saves on 18. The Blackhawks keep promising the rebuild is almost done, and the scoreboard keeps asking for another year's rent.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

SJS3STL2OTFinal: SJS 3, STL 2 OT

San Jose has decided regulation is for other teams. Connor McMichael gave St. Louis the lead 3:52 in, Tyler Toffoli tied it in the second off a feed from Michael Misa, and Dillon Dube put the Blues back in front with a shorthanded goal 99 seconds into the third. Collin Graf answered at 6:05, and then Darnell Nurse, of all people, ended it 63 seconds into overtime from Ivar Stenberg and Alexander Wennberg. Alex Nedeljkovic stopped 24 of 26 for the Sharks, and Joel Hofer made 24 saves on 27 for the Blues. Toffoli finished with a goal and an assist. The Sharks' first two wins this season also came in overtime, so the kids are learning to close; the Blues, meanwhile, scored a shorthanded go-ahead goal in the third on home ice and still let a team full of teenagers walk out with the extra point.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL7CGY3Final: COL 7, CGY 3

Colorado's defensemen outscored Calgary on their own. Devon Toews scored twice, Cale Makar added two goals and an assist, and Nathan MacKinnon had a goal and two helpers in a 7-3 romp at the Saddledome. Adam Klapka tied it 1-1 late in the first, and that was the last time this one looked like a contest: the Avs scored three in under five minutes of the second and two more early in the third. Jaden Schwartz scored twice, Noah Juulsen picked up his first point as an Avalanche player on the Toews goal, and Zachary L'Heureux dropped the gloves with Matt Coronato in the second. Mikael Backlund and Kevin Bahl scored 71 seconds apart in the third, which made it 6-3 for about a minute before Schwartz answered. Scott Wedgewood made 26 saves; Devin Cooley stopped 23 of 30. Calgary's season is starting to look less like a rebuild and more like a demolition with season tickets.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TOR3VGK4SOFinal: TOR 3, VGK 4 SO

Toronto led 3-0 eight and a half minutes into the game and still lost, in Vegas, with Mitch Marner on the other bench. Jack Roslovic scored 34 seconds in, Easton Cowan and Nick Paul followed, and then the Leafs did the thing. Mark Stone got one back late in the first, Brett Howden scored early in the second with Marner picking up an assist against his old team, and Jack Eichel tied it with an extra skater on at 3:58 of the second. After that, nobody scored for 56 minutes. Sergei Bobrovsky made 40 saves on 43 and dragged Toronto to a shootout; Adin Hill stopped 21 of 24. Braeden Bowman and Kirill Marchenko traded goals, Matthews, Nylander, McKenna and Tavares all missed, and rookie Trevor Connelly won it in the fifth round. A three-goal lead, a shootout and Marner on the winning side: it's every Leafs fan's recurring nightmare, now available in Nevada.

Thursday, October 8

Game recap

PIT3WSH5Final: PIT 3, WSH 5

Washington's home opener got interesting 23 seconds in, when Anthony Beauvillier scored on the first shift, and the Capitals never trailed in a 5-3 win over Pittsburgh. Tom Wilson ran the show with a goal and two assists, Pierre-Luc Dubois added a goal and an assist, and Alex Tuch's third of the season made it 4-1 midway through the second. Then the Penguins remembered they're the team that hung seven on Philly: Tommy Novak and Nick Robertson scored 3:56 apart to make it 4-3 before the second intermission. Ryan Leonard ended the drama with a power-play goal 3:55 into the third, set up by Jordan Kyrou and Cole Hutson. Logan Thompson stopped 27 of 30. Arturs Silovs stopped 22 of 27, the hockey version of holding the door for everyone. Pittsburgh has now lost two straight, and that 7-0 opener is starting to look less like a statement and more like a typo.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL2WPG3Final: COL 2, WPG 3

The Jets are playing without Connor Hellebuyck and, so far, without a care. Stuart Skinner stopped 32 of 34, and Kyle Connor scored with exactly one minute left in regulation to beat Colorado 3-2 and hand the Avalanche their first loss. Jaden Schwartz opened the scoring early in the second, Connor answered 70 seconds later, and Cole Perfetti put Winnipeg ahead late in the period. Fedor Svechkov tied it at 12:35 of the third with his first of the season, and this one looked headed for overtime until Connor buried his fifth goal in four games. Mark Scheifele and Dylan Samberg had two assists each. Mackenzie Blackwood saw only 19 shots and let three in, and MacKinnon, Makar and Necas combined for zero points on eight shots. Last season's best team walked into Winnipeg with a +9 and walked out with a lesson: the Jets don't even need their MVP goalie to make your stars disappear.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

EDM5ANA2Final: EDM 5, ANA 2

For one period Anaheim looked like a team that hands out six-year deals after 14 NHL games with total confidence: Beckett Sennecke scored twice on the power play and the Ducks led 2-0. Then the second period happened. Evan Bouchard scored 11 seconds in, Kasperi Kapanen tied it on the power play, and Edmonton kept going, with Bouchard's second plus goals from Vasily Podkolzin and Connor McDavid, five in the period for a 5-2 win. Leon Draisaitl had four assists, McDavid a goal and two, and Bouchard now leads the NHL with six goals, which is a lot for a defenseman and an insult to every forward in the league. Devon Levi stopped 29 of 31. Lukas Dostal was pulled after allowing five on 17 shots, and the Oilers won with 19 shots all night. The Ducks' first period was terrific. Unfortunately for them, hockey still has three.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →
