Wednesday, October 7

Game recap

NSH4TOR5OTFinal: NSH 4, TOR 5 OT

Nashville built a 3-0 lead in Toronto and then handed it back one goal at a time, like a gambler who doesn't know when to leave the table. Steven Stamkos scored on the power play, Nils Hoglander scored twice, and it was 3-0 just 3:03 into the second. Then the Leafs woke up: John Tavares (with an assist from Anthony Stolarz, of all people), William Nylander on the power play, and after Stamkos made it 4-2, Gavin McKenna scored his first NHL goal. Jack Roslovic tied it 8:54 into the third, and Auston Matthews ended it 4:46 into overtime from Nylander, finishing with a goal and three assists. Toronto outshot Nashville 37-25. Juuse Saros made 32 saves; Stolarz made 21. The Leafs are 2-2. Nashville, 1-1-1, led by three on the road and left with one point, which is the most Predators way to spend a Tuesday.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

CAR6MTL4Final: CAR 6, MTL 4

Montreal threw a home-opener party and the team that ended its season last spring showed up uninvited and ate all the food. The first period had five goals and no defense: Taylor Hall scored 2:25 in, Zachary Bolduc and Nick Suzuki answered inside two minutes, and Bolduc's power-play goal made it 3-2 Habs after one. Then Carolina took over. Sebastian Aho tied it on the power play, Mark Jankowski put the Canes ahead, and Hall's second made it 5-3 with eight minutes left. Juraj Slafkovsky got one back with the goalie pulled, and Andrei Svechnikov hit the empty net. Aho finished with a goal and two assists. Brandon Bussi, a surprise starter, won with 16 saves on 20; Jakub Dobes stopped 28 of 33. Carolina outshot Montreal 34-20. The Canadiens are 1-1-1 and have now allowed 12 goals in two games, which is a lot of pucks for one Bell Centre to watch go in.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

OTT3DET5Final: OTT 3, DET 5

Dylan Larkin asked to be traded this summer, lost the C, got booed at the opener, and then walked into his season debut and gave Detroit its first win. Hockey is a funny business. Tim Stützle opened it 2:44 in, Alex DeBrincat tied it 32 seconds later, and Larkin put the Wings ahead late in the first. Viktor Arvidsson scored on the power play and Justin Faulk made it 4-1 by 4:30 of the second. Drake Batherson and William Eklund pulled Ottawa within one, but DeBrincat finished it with a power-play empty-netter at 19:10 for his second of the night. Lucas Raymond had three assists, Larkin a goal and an assist, and rookie William Wallinder picked up a point in his NHL debut. John Gibson made 22 saves; Samuel Ersson made 31 on 35. Detroit is 1-2. Ottawa's perfect start lasted exactly two games, which is about one more than Senators fans had budgeted for.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

UTA5NJD3Final: UTA 5, NJD 3

Utah scored twice on the power play, and the Devils' defense went missing for the rest of it. Clayton Keller scored on the power play 1:57 in, Luke Evangelista answered on New Jersey's, and the teams traded goals until Nick Schmaltz's power-play goal (his fifth already) and Lawson Crouse's at 19:03 of the second made it 4-2. Jesper Boqvist got the Devils within one in the third, and Vincent Trocheck, playing through a lower-body injury, scored his first goal as a Mammoth to close it. Schmaltz had a goal and two assists, Mikhail Sergachev three assists. Evangelista scored both New Jersey goals, and Timo Meier fired eight shots for one assist. Brenden Dillon and Jack McBain fought in the third. Karel Vejmelka made 30 saves; Jake Allen stopped 26 of 31. Utah is 3-1. The Devils are 1-2 and minus-7, and the blue line is starting to look like a waiting room.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN2BUF3OTFinal: MIN 2, BUF 3 OT

Minnesota led 2-0 with 25 minutes left and then remembered it was in Buffalo, where nice leads go to die. Danila Yurov scored on the power play at 13:53 of the second and Maxim Shabanov added another 1:45 later. Noah Ostlund cut it in half early in the third, Tage Thompson tied it at 9:38 on a night he reached 400 points as a Sabre, and Owen Power won it 4:22 into overtime from Jiri Kulich and Thompson. Thompson fired nine shots, Power and Thompson each had a goal and an assist, and Colten Ellis won his first start with 18 saves on 20. Jesper Wallstedt stopped 25 of 28. Matt Boldy had seven shots and nothing to show for them, and Kirill Kaprizov went pointless in 25 minutes. The Sabres are 2-1. The Wild got a point, which is nice, but they also blew a two-goal third-period lead to Buffalo, which is the kind of thing a team should keep out of the group chat.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI2NYR5Final: NYI 2, NYR 5

Alexis Lafrenière got a hat trick, and two-thirds of it was delivered to an empty net 32 seconds apart. Nobody at MSG asked for a receipt. Oliver Bjorkstrand opened the scoring and Lafrenière made it 2-0 25 seconds into the second, but the Islanders tied it within five minutes on goals from Bo Horvat (power play) and Calum Ritchie. Bjorkstrand's power-play goal at 17:07 of the second was the winner, his second of the night and his first two as a Ranger. Lafrenière then scored at 18:22 and 18:54 of the third with Semyon Varlamov on the bench. He also had an assist. There were two fights: Brayden Schenn and J.T. Miller in the first, Bjorkstrand and Adam Pelech in the final seconds. Varlamov, in his first NHL game since November 2024, made 19 saves; Igor Shesterkin made 17. The Rangers have won four straight. The Islanders are 1-2 and lost the Battle of New York on a pair of empty nets.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL2CHI4Final: STL 2, CHI 4

Chicago finally won a hockey game, and it picked the home opener to do it, which is good showmanship from a team that hadn't shown much else. Mason McTavish gave St. Louis the lead late in the first. In the second, Sam Rinzel tied it on the power play and Anton Frondell put the Hawks ahead two minutes later. The last 69 seconds were a fire drill: Cole Smith scored shorthanded into the empty net, Connor McMichael answered on the power play with Hofer pulled, and Frank Nazar hit the empty net again with four seconds left. Nazar and Frondell each had a goal and an assist. Spencer Knight made 26 saves on 28; Joel Hofer stopped 17 of 19. Colton Parayko tied Barret Jackman for the most games by a Blues defenseman. St. Louis is 1-2 to close its opening road trip and just gave a 1-3 rebuild its first win of the year. That's charity, not hockey.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

VGK6SEA2Final: VGK 6, SEA 2

Vegas went to Seattle and treated the Kraken like a comp'd buffet. It was 5-0 before the second intermission: Victor Olofsson scored twice, Tomas Hertl on the power play, Mark Stone shorthanded, and Jack Eichel unassisted with 31 seconds left in the period. Hertl added another power-play goal in the third. Hertl (two goals, two assists) and Eichel (a goal, three assists) had four points each. Joey Daccord was pulled after allowing five on 21 shots; Philipp Grubauer stopped 6 of 7. Shane Wright and Jared McCann scored for Seattle. It got nasty late: Brandon Montour fought Stone and took 17 penalty minutes, Marc Gatcomb fought Ryan Winterton, and Ben Meyers was thrown out for boarding Olofsson, with a league hearing expected. Carter Hart made 25 saves. Vegas is 3-1. Seattle is 2-2, and the Kraken's best work of the night came after the game was already gone.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

FLA2LAK1Final: FLA 2, LAK 1

The Panthers needed four games and a cross-country flight to win one in regulation, but they got it, 2-1 in the Kings' home opener. Alex Laferriere scored with a minute left in the first for Los Angeles. Seth Jones tied it 3:49 into the second, and Matthew Tkachuk won it at 11:20 of the third from Sam Bennett. Jacob Markstrom stopped 19 of 20, and the Kings managed just 20 shots in their own building. Darcy Kuemper made 26 saves on 28 and deserved better. Garnet Hathaway and Joel Edmundson fought in the second. Artemi Panarin had four shots and no points. Florida is 2-0-2. Los Angeles is 0-2-1, one of two teams in the West still without a win, and its home crowd paid opening-night prices to watch 20 shots in 60 minutes.

Beauvillier scored 23 seconds in, and Wilson, Dubois, Tuch and Leonard added goals as Washington built a 4-1 lead and held on. Logan Thompson made 24 saves; Silovs stopped 22 of 27 for Pittsburgh. Ovechkin and Crosby were both held off the scoresheet.

News

Jamie Benn is six points from 1,000 for his career

The Stars captain has 994 career points after a goal and an assist against San Jose on Monday, so he could reach 1,000 on this road trip or soon after.

MIN
News

Spurgeon passes Ryan Suter for the most power-play points by a defenseman in Wild history

Jared Spurgeon's assist on Danila Yurov's power-play goal in Buffalo was his 139th power-play point, one more than Suter. He now holds every major scoring record for a Wild defenseman.

Jared McCann seen shoving a linesman from the bench in the Vegas game; no penalty called

Update: Beauvillier joins Strome and Ovechkin for the opener; McIlrath in if Matt Roy can't play

Dylan McIlrath would replace him.

New York RangersNYR7-3-1 · 15 pts30 shots

Puckline's Report

The Rangers keep treating Madison Square Garden like a members-only club, and Anaheim wasn't on the list: 5-2, and New York is 6-0 at home. Sean Durzi scored 78 seconds in, J.T. Miller added a power-play goal, Gabe Perreault made it 3-0, and Oliver Bjorkstrand scored twice in barely 12 minutes of ice time, the kind of efficiency Rangers fans usually only see at the ticket office. Alexis Lafrenière set up two, and Dylan Garand stopped 29 of 31 to keep the Shesterkin-less crease humming. Ville Husso made 25 saves on 30. The Ducks finally scored at 18:51 of the third, then again at 19:27 through A.J. Greer, two goals that changed nothing but the box score. That's three straight losses for Anaheim, a team that flew across the country to watch a show and forgot it was supposed to be in it.

Puckline's Report

Philadelphia scores 1.40 goals a game, so naturally it hung three on one of the highest-scoring teams in the league. Flyers 3, Avalanche 2, and that's two wins in three nights for a team that couldn't buy one for two weeks. Matvei Michkov scored twice, the first on the power play, and Trevor Zegras set up all three Flyers goals, including Noel Acciari's first of the season early in the third. Joseph Woll stopped 24 of 26, which is all Colorado managed to throw at him, and Nathan MacKinnon went 24 minutes without a point. Martin Necas and T.J. Hughes scored for the Avs, Hughes with five minutes left, but Mackenzie Blackwood (21 saves on 24) got no more help. A Philly lineup missing Tippett, Konecny and York did this. Colorado now flies to New Jersey to play again tonight, which is still a better trip than the one its offense just took.

Puckline's Report

The Maple Leafs finally stopped the bleeding, and it took a teenager to do it. Toronto beat San Jose 3-1 to end a three-game skid. Mason Marchment put the Sharks up in the first, Auston Matthews tied it on the power play with 12 seconds left in the second, and Gavin McKenna scored the winner on another power play early in the third, his third of the year. Nick Paul hit the empty net with 40 seconds left. Matthews finished with a goal and two assists, William Nylander shook off an illness to set up the winner, and Sergei Bobrovsky stopped 30 of 31. Yaroslav Askarov was excellent in a losing cause, 29 saves on 31, and Macklin Celebrini put five shots on goal for nothing. The Sharks are 4-4-1 and still haven't won a game in regulation: nine games in, and they're still waiting for a win that doesn't need extra time or a skills competition.

PIT 4–5 UTA

Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT3-6-1 · 7 pts19 shots
4
FinalDelta Center
5
Utah MammothUTA7-3-0 · 14 pts29 shots
1st2nd3rdTPIT1124UTA2215

Puckline's Report

Erik Karlsson finally scored a goal, and Pittsburgh still found a way to lose. His power-play goal 71 seconds in was his first of the season, and the Penguins promptly gave up five of the next six as Utah won 5-4. Clayton Keller, Kevin Stenlund, Nate Schmidt, Kailer Yamamoto and Nick Schmaltz scored for Utah, Schmaltz on the power play early in the third for a 5-2 lead. Then the Penguins remembered they had shooters: Egor Chinakhov and Declan Carlile made it 5-4 with five minutes left, and that was it. Utah outshot Pittsburgh 29-19, so Sebastian Cossa only had to stop 15 of 19, while Arturs Silovs made 24 saves on 29. Bryan Rust had two assists before leaving with a lower-body injury. That's four straight losses and a 3-6-1 record for a team built to squeeze one more run out of Sid and Geno, and so far the only thing it's squeezing is the panic button.

SJS @ MTL · 7:00 PM ET

San Jose SharksSJS4-4-1 · 9 PTSML +172
@7:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Centre Bell
SJS +172MLMTL -210
Montreal CanadiensMTL4-3-1 · 9 PTSML -210

Puckline Preview

The Sharks roll into the Bell Centre on the second night of a back-to-back, fresh off a 3-1 loss in Toronto where they won the chances and lost the special teams. San Jose is 4-4-1 and every one of those wins came in overtime or a shootout, which makes the Sharks the NHL's most dedicated fans of extra hockey. Macklin Celebrini leads them with 11 points and owns this building: he had two goals and an assist in a 4-2 win here last March, the second of San Jose's two wins over Montreal last season. Alex Nedeljkovic is projected to start after Yaroslav Askarov went last night, and Alexander Wennberg is questionable after getting hurt in Toronto.

Montreal has won three straight at home, and if this goes to a shootout, good luck: the Habs are 2-0 there and Zachary Bolduc is 2-for-2. Cole Caufield won Saturday's game in overtime, Nick Suzuki leads with 10 points, and the Canadiens confirmed Jakub Dobes gets the start in goal after Jacob Fowler started four of the last five. Chris Kreider, on the other hand, has gone five games without a point and lost his spot on the first power-play unit to Bolduc. Demidov and Matheson are still out. It's the Canadiens' last home game before Sunday's Heritage Classic in Winnipeg, so expect the Bell Centre to want a send-off.

By Puckline Prince

COL @ NJD · 7:00 PM ET

Colorado AvalancheCOL5-3-1 · 11 PTSML -105
@7:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Prudential Center
COL -105MLNJD -114
New Jersey DevilsNJD4-4-0 · 8 PTSML -114

Puckline Preview

Colorado scores 4.50 goals a game and still managed to lose 3-2 last night to a Philadelphia team that averages 1.40, which is the hockey version of a lion getting mugged by a goose. Now the Avs play the second half of a back-to-back in Newark, and they did it carrying 11 forwards and seven defensemen, with Nicolas Roy and Zachary L'Heureux left in Denver. Nathan MacKinnon has 16 points and was blanked in 24 minutes last night, and Scott Wedgewood is projected to start against his old team after Mackenzie Blackwood went in Philly.

The Devils have had three days to stew on a 4-2 loss in Washington, which came two days after they hung seven on the Rangers. Jack Hughes leads them with nine points, Arseny Gritsyuk has three goals in his last four games, and Jake Allen was in the starter's net at the morning skate on the night the Devils honour his 500th game, though Sheldon Keefe hasn't officially named him. Connor Brown finally makes his season debut and Luke Evangelista is back from his illness, so Stefan Noesen sits despite a three-game point streak. Anthony Mantha shook off his own bug and is projected on the third line. Seamus Casey and Nick Bjugstad are still out. These two split last season, a 4-3 Devils overtime win in Newark and an 8-4 Avalanche blowout in Denver two nights later, and old-timers in Jersey still haven't forgiven Colorado for Game 7 of the 2001 Final.

By Puckline Prince

ANA @ NYI · 7:00 PM ET

Anaheim DucksANA4-4-0 · 8 PTSML +128
@7:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · UBS Arena
ANA +128MLNYI -154
New York IslandersNYI4-3-1 · 9 PTSML -154

Puckline Preview

The Ducks' East Coast swing has gone about as well as their travel: a 15-hour day getting here, then a 5-2 loss at Madison Square Garden in which they trailed 5-0 before two goals in the final 69 seconds. That's three straight losses after a 4-1 start, and now it's the second night of a back-to-back on Long Island. Lukas Dostal is expected back in goal after Ville Husso took the loss last night. Leo Carlsson leads Anaheim with nine points and Beckett Sennecke has five goals, with Troy Terry and Ryan Poehling still out.

The Islanders have quietly become a wall. They've allowed 17 goals in eight games, their fewest that early since 2001, with an 86.7% penalty kill, and Ilya Sorokin sits at .940. Bo Horvat leads them with nine points and Matthew Schaefer has seven assists. The bad news is the medical list: Mathew Barzal has no return date, Alexander Romanov tore his ACL, and Calum Ritchie (4-6 weeks) and Matias Maccelli (2-4 weeks) joined them, so Mitchell Chaffee came up on an emergency recall to debut on the fourth line. Former Duck Kyle Palmieri moves up to Horvat's line. The teams split last season. Anaheim, meanwhile, has spent two days proving it can cross a continent faster than it can get a puck past a goalie.

By Puckline Prince

LAK @ WSH · 7:00 PM ET

Los Angeles KingsLAK0-4-2 · 2 PTSML +132
@7:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Capital One Arena
LAK +132MLWSH -160
Washington CapitalsWSH5-3-0 · 10 PTSML -160

Puckline Preview

Six games in, the Kings are 0-4-2 and the last winless team in the NHL, and they open a five-game road trip in a building where they've had no luck lately: Washington is 11-3-0 against Los Angeles since 2019-20 and won both meetings last season. The numbers behind the slump are grim. The Kings score two goals a game, shoot 4.71% at five-on-five and kill 61.9% of penalties, and Quinton Byfield, with two points in six games, has publicly owned his slow start. Help has arrived: Mats Zuccarello is back tonight on Byfield's line. Darcy Kuemper was first off the ice at the morning skate and looks like the starter against his old team, and Kevin Fiala is still out.

The Capitals go for a third straight win to open a five-game homestand, and Alex Ovechkin sits on 761 career assists, one short of Nicklas Backstrom's franchise record of 762. Rookie Ilya Protas has five points, Pierre-Luc Dubois misses another game with an illness, and Matt Roy is back on the top pair after coming off injured reserve. Logan Thompson gets the start in goal. The Kings arrive needing a win so badly they'd probably take one in a shootout against the Zamboni.

By Puckline Prince

TOR @ CBJ · 7:00 PM ET

Toronto Maple LeafsTOR4-4-2 · 10 PTSML +128
@7:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Nationwide Arena
TOR +128MLCBJ -154
Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ3-4-0 · 6 PTSML -154

Puckline Preview

Matthew Knies gets his first crack at the team that traded him. The Leafs sent him to Columbus on Sept. 29 in the deal that brought Kirill Marchenko (and the injured Elvis Merzlikins) to Toronto, and Knies insists tonight isn't about payback. Fine, but he has six points and none since his second game, so a little payback wouldn't hurt. The Blue Jackets' power play is 2-for-17 and they managed 14 shots in Sunday's 2-1 loss in Minnesota, so the offense could use whatever emotion it can find. Kent Johnson has been their hot hand, and Jet Greaves, who shut out the Rangers on Saturday, is projected in goal.

Toronto plays the second night of a back-to-back after snapping a three-game skid with a 3-1 win over San Jose. Gavin McKenna scored the power-play winner, Auston Matthews had three points, and the penalty kill has killed 21 straight. Anthony Stolarz starts, per Jim Hiller, with an .875 save percentage in three starts. The Leafs are still without John Tavares, Chris Tanev and Max Domi. Last November's meeting went to overtime, a 2-1 Leafs win in which a Zach Werenski goal came off the board on an offside challenge, the kind of thing that happens to Columbus a lot.

By Puckline Prince

WPG @ STL · 8:00 PM ET

Winnipeg JetsWPG4-2-2 · 10 PTSML +118
@8:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Enterprise Center
WPG +118MLSTL -142
St Louis BluesSTL3-4-1 · 7 PTSML -142

Puckline Preview

Blues fans don't need a reminder, so here's one anyway: Game 7 of the 2025 first round, St. Louis up a goal late, and Cole Perfetti tied it with 1.6 seconds left before Adam Lowry won it in double overtime. That's the scar tissue in this one. Winnipeg also won the last meeting, 3-2 in St. Louis in April, and the Blues are 2-4-1 in their last seven against the Jets.

The Jets are 4-2-2 but have dropped two straight, and the Connor Hellebuyck standoff is still the loudest thing about them: his suspension is reported to end Friday, and ESPN says at least three teams are still talking trade with Winnipeg. Stuart Skinner (3-0-1) keeps the crease warm. Kyle Connor has eight goals, and Mark Scheifele has a five-game point streak and sits five goals shy of Dale Hawerchuk's franchise record. Josh Morrissey is on IR and Vladislav Namestnikov is out. St. Louis has lost two straight too and has an IR list long enough to need a table of contents: Krug, Dube, Mailloux, Tucker, Toropchenko and Johnston. Mason McTavish carries a six-game point streak, and Joel Hofer is projected in goal against a Jets penalty kill that ranks 20th.

BOS @ DAL · 8:00 PM ET

Boston BruinsBOS7-2-0 · 14 PTSML +140
@8:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · American Airlines Center
BOS +140MLDAL -170
Dallas StarsDAL4-3-1 · 9 PTSML -170

Puckline Preview

Boston goes for six straight wins against the stingiest team in hockey. The Stars allow 1.50 goals a game, fewest in the league, and Jake Oettinger, who starts again tonight, is sitting on a .952 save percentage after Saturday's 4-0 shutout in Chicago. The catch is the other end: Dallas ranks 28th in scoring, and losing Matt Duchene for about three months after core-muscle surgery didn't help. Now the blue line takes a hit too: Esa Lindell is out at least a week after blocking a shot in Chicago, so Kyle Capobianco makes his season debut next to Miro Heiskanen. Jason Robertson has points in seven straight games against Boston, and Roope Hintz is expected to play through a hand issue.

The Bruins are 7-2 and +15. David Pastrnak has 12 points and a point in eight straight games against Dallas, Matt Poitras has a five-game point streak, and Jeremy Swayman (6-1-0, .934) gets the start. Pavel Zacha is back from his upper-body injury between Morgan Geekie and Pastrnak, and Nikita Zadorov returns after getting benched for discipline last game, with his agent weighing in publicly, which is about as Bruins-defenseman as a storyline gets. The last meeting, March 31, was a 6-3 Boston win in which Viktor Arvidsson scored a hat trick, two of them into an empty net. Dallas has the goalie and the defense; what it needs is someone willing to score on purpose.

By Puckline Prince

MIN @ EDM · 9:00 PM ET

Minnesota WildMIN6-2-1 · 13 PTSML +112
@9:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Rogers Place
MIN +112MLEDM -134
Edmonton OilersEDM6-1-1 · 13 PTSML -134

Puckline Preview

Two of the hottest players on the planet share the ice tonight. Kirill Kaprizov leads the league with 10 goals in nine games, the fastest anyone in Wild history has gotten there, and carries a six-game point streak. Connor McDavid has 23 points in eight games, which is the kind of start that makes the rest of the league's scoring race look like a participation trophy. McDavid has points in 10 of his last 11 against Minnesota, but the Oilers as a team have lost 14 of their last 18 to the Wild, including all three meetings last season. The last one, Jan. 31, was a 7-3 Wild win in Edmonton in which Jesper Wallstedt made 39 saves and Tristan Jarry got pulled. Wallstedt is projected again tonight. Edmonton is going with Devon Levi, which spares Jarry the rerun.

Minnesota is 6-2-1 and first in the Central despite a medical list that reads like a depth chart: Brock Faber, Filip Gustavsson, both Folignos and Nico Sturm are out, and Jared Spurgeon is questionable after travelling with the team. Edmonton is 6-1-1 and keeps Saturday's lineup: Ryan Nugent-Hopkins has been practicing at second-line center but stays on IR for another game, and Jason Dickinson is still out.

By Puckline Prince

DET @ SEA · 9:40 PM ET

Detroit Red WingsDET3-3-2 · 8 PTSML -110
@9:40 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Climate Pledge Arena
DET -110MLSEA -110
Seattle KrakenSEA5-3-1 · 11 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

The last time these two met, Oct. 9 in Detroit, the Red Wings outshot Seattle 16-3 early and led 2-1, and then the Kraken scored three goals in 3:05, Frederick Gaudreau twice, to chase John Gibson on the way to a 6-3 win. Philipp Grubauer made 37 saves that night, and he's projected again tonight after Joey Daccord gave up eight in Florida on Saturday. Grubauer is 5-1-1 lifetime against Detroit. Seattle has lost two straight but scores 3.78 a game, and the Kakko-Catton-Wright line has combined for seven goals and 18 points. Brandon Montour is out of the lineup again and Ryan Lindgren is on IR.

Detroit has points in four straight (2-0-2), and Todd McLellan confirmed Daniil Tarasov starts, which is brave: Tarasov is 0-3-0 lifetime against the Kraken with an .830 save percentage. This is the Wings' first real road trip after seven of their first eight at home. Alex DeBrincat leads them with nine points fresh off his seven-year, $91 million extension, and the Dylan Larkin trade-request saga is still hanging over the room. Marco Kasper and Mason Appleton didn't travel, and J.T. Compher is questionable. The Wings say they wanted this rematch; last time, their lead lasted until Seattle decided to try.

By Puckline Prince

CAR @ VAN · 10:00 PM ET

Carolina HurricanesCAR7-2-1 · 15 PTSML -300
@10:00 PM ETTue Oct 20 · Rogers Arena
CAR -300MLVAN +240
Vancouver CanucksVAN2-7-1 · 5 PTSML +240

Puckline Preview

The last time Vancouver saw Carolina, Oct. 8 in Raleigh, Logan Stankoven scored a natural hat trick with an even-strength, a power-play and a short-handed goal, Sean Walker set up four, Kevin Lankinen got pulled after two periods, and the Hurricanes went 3-for-3 on the power play in a 7-2 win. The Canucks haven't won since. They're 2-7-1 on a seven-game winless run, took one point from 12 on their road trip, allow 4.50 goals a game and own the league's worst penalty kill at 58.1%. Leevi Meriläinen is expected in goal, Marco Rossi is questionable with an illness, and Thatcher Demko is on IR. The Canucks also honour the late broadcaster John Garrett tonight.

Carolina is 7-2-1, though its seven-game win streak ended Sunday in Calgary. Sebastian Aho has 14 points, Jesperi Kotkaniemi has scored in back-to-back games and is getting more power-play and penalty-kill time, and the Canes are without Taylor Hall, Jordan Staal, Mark Jankowski and Seth Jarvis, with Bradly Nadeau and Felix Unger Sorum up from Chicago. Pyotr Kochetkov (5-0, 1.78) is the likely starter per the team's preview, though Carolina Hockey Now expects Brandon Bussi. Vancouver's penalty kill against a top-10 power play is the kind of matchup the Canucks would rather watch from the press box.

By Puckline Prince

TBL @ VGK · 10:30 PM ET

Tampa Bay LightningTBL6-2-0 · 12 PTSML -110
@10:30 PM ETTue Oct 20 · T-Mobile Arena
TBL -110MLVGK -110
Vegas Golden KnightsVGK8-2-0 · 16 PTSML -110

Puckline Preview

The nightcap is a heavyweight card on national TV. Vegas is 8-2, 5-1-0 at home and +18, the best goal difference in the league, after three straight wins by a combined 17-6. Jack Eichel has 18 points and Mark Stone seven goals. The weak spot is the blue line: Alex Pietrangelo is on LTIR, and Parker Wotherspoon and Lukas Cormier are out too, so the Golden Knights are patching their defense with whatever's left in the gift shop. Carter Hart is projected in goal.

Tampa Bay is 6-2 with two straight wins and opens a three-game western trip here. Brandon Hagel leads the Lightning with 11 points, Yanni Gourde is out after hip surgery, and Andrei Vasilevskiy is projected to start; he's 8-5-3 lifetime against Vegas. Nikita Kucherov treats this matchup like a personal holiday, with 26 points in 14 career games against the Golden Knights. The last meeting, Nov. 6, 2025, went Tampa's way 6-3 in Vegas after the Bolts fell behind 2-0 and were outshot 15-3 in the first period; Kucherov and Hagel scored two each, and Tampa won both meetings last season. Vegas fans, remember: the house always wins, except apparently when the house is playing the Lightning.

By Puckline Prince
